protocol.record: docs/decisions/scoring-protocol.md (version 1; read as the text of #640, comment 6127513444, accepted by Eleonora in comment 6131185033; its merge is hers)
protocol.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (grid_crps, upper_tail_twcrps, day_scores, fill_missing, paired_tests) and repo_model.protocol_benchmarks (b1_forecast, b2_forecast)
protocol.primary_score: grid CRPS (twice the mean pinball loss over the 23 levels), averaged with equal weight over h = 1 to 5, one number per decision day
protocol.difference: d = S(benchmark) - S(candidate); positive favours the candidate; skill = mean(d) / mean(S(benchmark))
protocol.interval: stationary bootstrap, mean block length 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 634, one-sided 95% (the lower bound of mean(d); the upper bound of skill); Diebold-Mariano with Newey-West lag 10 beside it
protocol.not_applied: the checkpoints, the O'Brien-Fleming spending and the verdict rule (sections 6 and 8) apply to confirmation days; development days give a score and an interval, never a verdict. Holm is not applied: no claim is tested

scoring.last_decision_day_rule: a decision day is scored when every one of its five target days is on or before 2025-12-31 and has a published outcome
scoring.outcome: the panel's spread_bps on the target day (the published panel, digest 4ddc3882...), not re-derived from first-published vintages

base.reading: the published funding declaration's features (scripts/live_record.py CRPS_FEATURES); treasury_settlement is dropped at h >= 2 when read as published (published_features), kept at every lead when announcement-dated

timing.settlement: treasury_settlement dated from the announcement (metadata/settlement_announcement_dating.json, the 'both' arm of #541)
timing.h41: reserve_balances and tga read per H.4.1 release (metadata/h41_release_dating.json, #541)

columns.tax_date: the tax-date window on market days (data.tax_date_market_days, #538); the panel is built with scripts/tax_date_market_days.py
columns.reserve_scarcity_state: the scarcity state read per leg (#571)
columns.iorb_days_to_announced_change: days to that change (#579); empty when no change is announced, which the gbm imputes
columns.satiation_dist_roll: the rolling satiation distance (#587, #598), constants unchanged
columns.sofr_p99_iorb_bps: the tail-spread level: the previous day's SOFR 99th percentile above IORB (#601)

new.source: scripts/pressure_v1_1.py panel, scripts/measurement_fields.py panel and scripts/satiation_distance_598.py panel, each run under scripts/tax_date_market_days.py; off in every published declaration, switched on for these runs only (satiation_distance_598.switched_on)
new.iorb_leads: the announced IORB change is public one panel day ahead (metadata/sources.json), so iorb_announced_change_bps and iorb_days_to_announced_change are inputs at h = 1 only; at h = 2 to 5 variants a, b and c run without them, as iorb_every_day_579.py does. Amended after the h = 1 walks and before any score, when the as-of rule refused the columns at h >= 2
new.not_included: #622's lag fix is on main (#623 merged) and is in the distance column as built; no other input is added; the ON RRP rate, the SRF rate and the H.8 series belong to the liquidity repository

a_published_new.label: (a) the published funding declaration with the new inputs
a_published_new.model: gbm on the published features plus the new inputs, nested conformal PID calibration as the published distribution (cli_eval 'gbm', --calibration conformal_pid_nested)
a_published_new.grid_reading: the published model forecasts five levels; its law is put on the protocol's 23 by the linear law of the gbm exceedance (spread_distribution_632.quantile_at: linear between the fitted quantiles, continued at the outer segments' slopes). A reading, not a decision: see 'questions'

b_gbm_new.label: (b) gbm quantiles with the new inputs
b_gbm_new.model: ml.fit_gradient_boosted_quantiles at the 23 levels, no calibration, the published model's settings (random_state, min_samples_leaf), the base features plus the new inputs, every day, directly at each lead

c_two_part_new.label: (c) two-part form, chosen from #632's step 1
c_two_part_new.model: ml.pressure_spread_distribution_exceedance, structure 'two_part' at the protocol's 23 levels: the risk-date part as in #632 on the inputs of risk_gbm+settle+h41+dist_roll plus iorb_announced_change_bps, and an every-day part on spread_bps, sofr_p75_iorb_bps, sofr_p99_iorb_bps, satiation_dist_roll, iorb_announced_change_bps and reserve_scarcity_state. A day whose every-day inputs are not all public has no forecast and is scored as B1's (protocol section 11)
c_two_part_new.chosen_because: #632's step 1 (docs/pivot/spread-distribution-result.md): the two-part form was the one that beat as-of persistence at every lead

controls.published: the published funding declaration as it stands, five levels (docs/runs/published_distribution_daily_h*.json, reproduced here by a re-run of the same walk on the same panel, which must match to the byte before it is used): B3 and the ablation parent of (a)
controls.gbm_funding: ml.fit_gradient_boosted_quantiles at the 23 levels on the published features only, uncalibrated: the phase 2 gbm re-scored under the protocol, and the ablation parent of (b)

benchmarks.B3: the published funding declaration (control 'published'), on the grid by the reading above

pairs.benchmarks: every variant and control against B1, B2 and B3

also: pinball loss at the levels 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 0.95 (the fixed grid of contract.QUANTILE_LEVELS), averaged over the leads
50% and 90% central interval coverage (levels 0.25 and 0.75; 0.05 and 0.95)

Brier score of P(spread > 0, +2, +5, +10 bp) read off the distribution, against the calendar-climatology and the persistence-logistic models fitted at the same thresholds and lead (the whole-basis-point event of docs/decisions/pressure-probability.md)

splits.regime: metadata/evaluation_splits.json regimes, by the decision day: 2018-19, 2020, 2021-23, 2024, 2025-26 are called out. These regimes were drawn after the fact; the protocol (section 7) makes no split a pass requirement, and none is here
splits.day_type: the pressure-day type of metadata/evaluation_splits.json (SplitDeclaration.reporting_day_type) of the target day: a decision day's score on a type is the mean over those of its leads whose target is of that type
splits.upper_tail_reported_separately: the Brier table at 0, +2, +5, +10 bp and the key secondary

variant_count: spread-forecast variants scored in development before this directive: phase 2, three distribution models (gbm uncalibrated, gbm cross-conformal, the published nested-PID declaration); #632, two variants. This directive adds three declared variants (a, b, c) and one re-fitted control (gbm_funding), so four new fits and nine in all
questions: How the five-level published declaration is put on the protocol's 23-level grid (B3 and variant a). protocol_benchmarks.b3_forecast refuses any grid but the protocol's and says this is hers (#655). This measurement reads it by the linear law stated above and reports it as a reading
Whether the outcome should be re-derived from first-published vintages (section 11) rather than the panel's spread_bps

the ON RRP rate, SRF rate and H.8 inputs (liquidity repository)
